subject: computer-science
title: High vs Low Level and Translators
welcome_lead: From human-readable to machine code — and the tools in between.
meta_desc: A-Level CS: high vs low level, compilers, interpreters and assemblers.
final_note: Choose the right level for the job — performance vs productivity.

concepts.def: A language close to human thought, like Python or Java.
Assembly or machine code — close to the hardware.
A translator that converts source code to machine code in advance.
A translator that executes source code line by line.
A translator from assembly language to machine code.
Intermediate code run by a virtual machine, e.g. JVM bytecode.

walkthroughs.body_html: High-level languages abstract away registers and memory — one line may do a great deal. Low-level code (assembly, machine code) maps almost one-to-one to CPU instructions, giving control at the cost of productivity.
A compiler translates the whole program before running it — fast at runtime, slow to start. An interpreter executes line by line — slower at runtime but quicker to test and debug.
Languages like Java compile to bytecode that runs on a virtual machine. This gives portability ('write once, run anywhere') and just-in-time optimisation, blending compiler and interpreter benefits.
